hints.title: Downward Path Constraints
hints.text: Any valid path from an ancestor to a descendant may contain at most one duplicate value. Tracking the depths where each value was seen helps identify where valid downward segments begin.

hints.title: Prefix Sums and Depth Map
hints.text: Perform a recursive traversal while maintaining the cumulative edge weights along the path. Store the depth of previous occurrences of each node value.

hints.title: Boundary Maintenance
hints.text: Keep track of the two largest previous duplicate depths. The path start index must be at least the smaller of the two largest conflict depths to ensure at most one duplicated value exists.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import sys

sys.setrecursionlimit(200000)

class Solution:
    def longestSpecialPath(self, edges: list[list[int]], nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v, w in edges:
            graph[u].append((v, w))
            graph[v].append((u, w))

        max_length = 0
        min_nodes = 1

        prefix = [0]
        last_seen = {}

        def dfs(u: int, prev: int, left_boundary: list[int]) -> None:
            nonlocal max_length, min_nodes

            val = nums[u]
            prev_depth = last_seen.get(val, 0)
            last_seen[val] = len(prefix)

            if prev_depth != 0:
                left_boundary.append(prev_depth)
                left_boundary.sort()
                left_boundary = [left_boundary[-2], left_boundary[-1]]

            start_idx = left_boundary[0]
            length = prefix[-1] - prefix[start_idx]
            nodes = len(prefix) - start_idx

            if length > max_length:
                max_length = length
                min_nodes = nodes
            elif length == max_length:
                min_nodes = min(min_nodes, nodes)

            for v, w in graph[u]:
                if v != prev:
                    prefix.append(prefix[-1] + w)
                    dfs(v, u, list(left_boundary))
                    prefix.pop()

            last_seen[val] = prev_depth

        dfs(0, -1, [0, 0])
        return [max_length, min_nodes]
```

variables: N: number of nodes in the tree
complexity.notes: Each tree node and edge is visited once with constant-time boundary updates.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all ancestor pairs naively requires O(N^2) operations, which times out for large trees.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining recursion state and boundary pairs uses linear space for linear execution time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize that maintaining the top two conflict depths enables constant-time window bounds during tree traversal.
